<thought>We need the number of aromatic carbons in the unknown molecule. The only way to infer this without a structural description is to obtain its 13C NMR spectrum and count the signals that fall in the typical aromatic carbon chemical shift range (≈120–150 ppm). This will give the count of distinct aromatic carbon environments, which for most molecules corresponds to the total number of aromatic carbons (assuming no symmetry that makes signals overlap). We'll request the 13C NMR spectrum for the sample at hand.</thought>
